subject: CityHealth MAP: evidence ledger & acceptance proofpoints
messages:
From: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@cityhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cityhealth.com
Date: 2026-08-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP & acceptance tests for pilot (CityHealth)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. The leadership team at CityHealth liked Redwood's latency/cost story and wants a short mutual action plan that ties concrete acceptance tests to our procurement milestones.

Can you send a MAP draft that:
- Lists success KPIs (throughput, 95p latency, error rate),
- Defines exit gates for pilot -> prod,
- Enumerates concrete evidence artifacts we can hand to our audit/compliance team (logs, SOC 2 snapshot, retention configs), and
- Shows who on Redwood will own each acceptance check?

We need this by EOW to keep the procurement clock moving.

Cheers,
Sarah
Sarah Lopez
VP Product, CityHealth

--
Attachment: RFP-AppendixA.pdf (referenced)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@cityhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & acceptance tests for pilot (CityHealth)

Hi Sarah — great to hear the demo landed. Attached is a first-pass MAP (CityHealth_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short acceptance-test catalog (acceptance-test-catalog.pdf). High-level summary below.

Summary (short):
- Success KPIs: 95th percentile < 180ms for single-turn generation at 1 concurrent request per user; end-to-end pipeline error rate < 0.5% over a 24h rolling window; semantic accuracy (top-N recall) >= 92% on your sample eval set.
- Exit gates (pilot -> prod):
  1) Stability gate: 14 consecutive days meeting latency + error KPIs in staging with representative traffic.
  2) Data & security gate: evidence of KMS integration + passing of our checklist items 1–6 (listed in sheet).
  3) Cost predictability gate: 7-day forecast within 15% of actual observed spend at expected load.
- Evidence artifacts: per-token latency traces, aggregated error logs, SOC 2 snapshot, routing policy config, model verison manifest, and a signed operational runbook. Each artifact is mapped to an acceptance check in column D of the MAP spreadsheet.

Owners:
- Kimberly (Customer Success / partner lead): overall MAP owner, acceptance coordinator.
- Marissa (Solutions): technical verification tests + smoke scripts.
- Aditya (SRE): runtime perf trace collection + KV cache verification.

Next steps:
1) We put a draft MAP in the shared Drive (link below).
2) Can you confirm which of the acceptance tests CityHealth will own vs Redwood will provide evidence for? I added a proposed split in column F.
3) If that looks ok, we’ll lock the acceptance-test cadence (daily/weekly) and start the staging run.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cCityHealthEvidence

Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: CityHealth_MAP_v1.xlsx, acceptance-test-catalog.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-21T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: acceptance test owners & smoke scripts (CityHealth)

Kimberly / Aditya — looping you in with a suggested verification plan. I pulled the sample eval set Sarah shared and sketched the smoke scripts. Key notes:

- Smoke script A (latency sanity): 500 short prompts across 10 client profiles, target 95p < 180ms; results include tracing id output for correlation. Owner: Aditya.
- Smoke script B (accuracy): 1k prompt pairs measured against CityHealth eval labels; owner: Marissa. Metric: top-1 F1 and top-3 recall.
- Logging & Evidence: we will export a daily artifact bundle (gzip) that includes token-level latency CSV, service logs (30 days window), and model manifest.json. Owner: Aditya (export infra), Marissa (artifact validation).
- Compliance checklist: Kimberly to coordinate KMS proof, SOC 2 report, and redaction policy confirmation with their Security contact.

I recommend we add an acceptance gate that requires a run of both smoke scripts in staging with live synthetic traffic for 72 continuous hours before starting the 14-day stability window — this reduces churn from infra flakiness.

I attached a short runbook draft to the Drive under /evidence/runbooks/CityHealth_smoke_v1.md and updated the MAP spreadsheet.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment referenced: CityHealth_smoke_v1.md (Drive)

From: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@cityhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cityhealth.com
Date: 2026-08-25T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CityHealth MAP: evidence ledger & acceptance proofpoints

Kimberly — this is very helpful, thank you. Procurement reviewed the artifacts and asked one clarification: will Redwood provide a signed artifact bundle daily during the staging runs (we need a channel for auditor ingestion)?

We also agreed internally that CityHealth will own the accuracy tests (Marissa's script B) and Redwood will own latency/error traces and the export. Please add that ownership split into column F and we’ll route to our security team for a final check.

If you can add a DocuSign link for the MAP acceptance handshake, we can move to a PO.

Thanks,
Sarah
